notes:
Context: mid-market SaaS (B2B product analytics) building in-app semantic search + recommendations. Core ask: fast, cheap embeddings pipeline that integrates with their vector DB and supports nightly batch jobs.

Key quotes from calls:
- 'We need predictable latency under load — 200 qps in peak window, p95 <150ms for search.' — CTO
- 'If Hosted API works and pricing scales, we will pilot; otherwise we want a Dedicated plan.' — Head of Product

POC observations (shorthand):
- Hosted API easy to onboard, SDK + quickstart successful.
- Embedding throughput: parallel batch runner works but hit rate limits; want guidance on batching configs and autoscaling.
- Vector DB connector: using Pinecone today; need canonical connector + docs for data sync and retry semantics.
- Nightly batch: target ~500k doc embeddings/day; window 3–4 hrs; prefer fast bulk endpoint or bulk upload support.
- Security: require SSO, SOC2 attestation, audit logging, and EU data residency for parts of index. KMS mandatory for Dedicated.

Commercial: mid-market budget, price sensitive — emphasized cost/embedding and unit economics. Looking at ~$50k-150k ARR depending on Dedicated sizing.

Next steps (internal): Jordan to run final performance matrix with Priya, capture Dedicated sizing, produce pricing options (monthly commit vs burst), handoff to procurement in May.
poc_summary: POC objective: validate Hosted API for embeddings + semantic search at production scale; measure ingest throughput and query latency; validate vector DB integration with Pinecone; test nightly batch embedding pipeline. Acceptance criteria: ingest 500k docs/day in a 4-hour window (sustained embedding rate ~35–45 embeds/sec), semantic search qps 150–250 with median latency <80ms and p95 <150ms, and end-to-end sync to Pinecone with <5% failure rate on first-run batches.
technical_requirements: Sustained embedding throughput required during window: ~40 embeds/sec
Vector DB: Pinecone (namespace per customer), retry semantics, upserts
Residency: EU-only subset for customer PII indexes
pricing_notes: They are comparing per-embedding cost (hosted) vs Dedicated baseline (monthly commit). Important to show cost delta when using batching, K/V caching, and quantized model variants. Procurement cares about predictable commit + burst buffer.
